matchupAnalysis: A light-heavyweight powder keg: the model finishes 77% of the time, decisions land only 23%, and the round-1 finish rate of 52.7% is the highest on the card. Both men carry big KO threats (Zhang +1.88, Menifield +1.07) into vulnerable chins (Zhang −0.63, Menifield −1.05). The separating number is the KO-threat differential. Zhang's +1.88 is one of the largest on the card and it points straight at Menifield's −1.05 chin — the worse of two suspect chins. Menifield, 39, has been stopped in 57% of his losses, most recently a first-round KO by Volkan Oezdemir. Zhang's own chin is a genuine liability (KO'd by Johnny Walker last time out), so the first clean exchange can go either way — but Zhang gets to the trigger faster and hits harder.

Sample warning: Zhang has only 5 division fights and ~20 minutes of UFC cage time, so the model leans on a 100%-KO finish profile and a strong pre-UFC record more than on stable UFC composites. Menifield's 19 fights give a far more stable read on his decline. Zhang's KO/TKO win share of 50.3% is the single dominant bucket in the fight; Menifield's most credible answer is his own power (10.5% KO).

synopsis.body: Modal terminal state is a Zhang KO/TKO (50.3%), most likely round one (fight R1 finish 52.7%). Realistic upset path is symmetrical — Menifield's +1.07 KO threat into Zhang's own glass chin, his 10.5% KO equity — but Zhang's +1.88 threat wins the exchange more often. Moderate confidence: two suspect chins and a thin Zhang sample make this higher-variance than 72% suggests.

Pavlovich's own chin (−0.32) is only average, so a single clean shot can change the night.

synopsis.body: Most likely terminal state is a Pavlovich KO/TKO (50.1%), most likely round one. matchupAnalysis: The lopsided structural read of the card, and it rests on one number: Harris's chin composite of −1.92, one of the lowest in the batch, against Matthews's +1.39 KO threat. The chin-vs-chin gap is a 2.28z chasm (+0.37 vs −1.92). Matthews also owns output (+0.88 vs +0.39), grappling (+0.49 vs +0.11) and wrestling defense (+0.39 vs +0.02). The model lands Matthews at 81%.

Harris's only structural pluses are reach (+1.39 vs −0.17) and a slight power edge (+0.21 vs −0.23). Notably, Matthews's own power composite is negative (−0.23); his elevated KO threat is almost entirely a product of Harris's vulnerability, not Matthews's punching power — a reminder that KO threat is a matchup quantity, not a fighter trait. Harris, 39, comes off the longest layoff on the card (502 days) and two recent KO losses (Ponzinibbio, Khaos Williams); the model reads his chin as a structural cliff, not a blip.

Matthews's win equity splits between a decision his volume earns (34.4%, his largest single bucket) and a KO the chin gap invites (33.2%) — combined finish equity 46.6%. Harris is a career finisher (75% finish rate, 50% by submission), and his most realistic path is a submission on the mat (11.2%) or landing his reach-and-power early before the chin is tested (4.7% KO). Everything that requires him to absorb a clean Matthews shot points the other way.

synopsis.body: Modal terminal state is a Matthews decision (34.4%) or KO/TKO (33.2%) — together 68% of all sims. Realistic upset path is Harris's career submission game catching Matthews in a scramble (11.2%, his largest bucket) or a reach-and-power shot before his −1.92 chin is tested — small, and fading at 39 off a 502-day layoff. High-confidence Matthews.

matchupAnalysis: The most interesting fight on the card to read, and the favorite depends on how you weight the data. Run in all-fights mode — pooling Perez's full body of work — the model lands Perez 62% / Sumudaerji 38%. Perez's edges are power (+1.46 vs +0.10, a 1.36z gap) and, more surprisingly, grappling (+1.00 vs −0.34) with a +0.81 submission threat. Those two together make his win column finish-heavy: his submission share (24.8%) is actually his largest single bucket, ahead of decision (23.5%) and KO (13.7%).

Sumudaerji is not without a case — he wins the two biggest geometry/engine levers decisively: reach +1.76 vs −1.10 (a 2.87z gap, the largest in the fight) and cardio +1.15 vs −0.73 (a 1.88z gap), plus a chin edge (+0.51 vs −0.36). If he keeps it at range and turns it into a track meet, his volume banks rounds — his 25.5% decision share is his largest single bucket, and the fight reaches the judges 49% of the time. The decision edge is only mildly his way (+0.30), reflecting a real but narrow path.

The structural tension is range-and-cardio (Sumudaerji) vs power-and-grappling (Perez). Perez, 34, has an 83% finished-in-loss rate and poor cardio (−0.73), so his window is the early-to-middle rounds where his power and scrambles are freshest; Sumudaerji's is the championship-pace third. Perez's higher Elo (1768 vs 1656) and fuller, more finish-oriented record are why the all-fights read tips to him — note that a flyweight-only view of Sumudaerji flips the favorite.

synopsis.body: Most likely terminal states are a Perez submission (24.8%) and a Perez decision (23.5%); combined Perez finish equity is 38.5%. Realistic upset path is Sumudaerji's +2.87z reach and +1.88z cardio turning it into a range-and-volume decision — his 25.5% decision share is his largest bucket. Lower confidence: this favorite is the most settings-sensitive on the card, and Perez's edge leans on his power plus a grappling profile that only his fuller record credits.

matchupAnalysis: A clean striker-vs-grappler split, and the grappler holds the bigger levers. Amorim owns grappling (+1.02 vs −0.36, a 1.38z gap), a +1.15 sub threat (her largest weapon), and a commanding reach edge (+1.44 vs −1.28, a 2.72z gap — the largest geometric mismatch in the fight). She also exploits the one hole in Loma's game: Loma's wrestling defense is only +0.17 against Amorim's grappling. GBM and hand-tuned agree almost exactly (25.2% cal, 24.7% HT) — a low-parameter-sensitivity read.

Loma is the better pure striker — output +0.92 vs +0.23, chin +0.76 vs −0.03 — and if this stayed standing for fifteen minutes she would win the boxing. But she brings no power (KO threat −0.76) and, more importantly, no clear way to keep it standing: the 2.72z reach gap lets Amorim close on her terms, and the grappling differential means most clinch exchanges end on the canvas. The −0.35 decision edge and 31% ground share both lean Amorim.

Amorim is a finisher's finisher — a 100% career finish rate, 75% by submission, three straight first-or-second-round subs (Viana, Demopoulos, McKenna) before a decision loss to Mizuki. The model reflects it: her submission win share of 37.3% is the single largest bucket on the entire card, and her combined finish equity is 43.3%. Loma's path is to stuff the takedowns and bank rounds on volume — her 20.2% decision share is her largest bucket — but +0.17 wrestling defense is a thin reed against +1.02 grappling.

synopsis.body: Modal terminal state is an Amorim submission (37.3%) — the largest single bucket on the whole card — with a decision (24.7%) behind it; combined finish equity 43.3%. Realistic upset path is Loma keeping it standing and out-volume-ing her to a decision (20.2%, her largest bucket), where her +0.92 output and +0.76 chin would tell — but the 2.72z reach gap makes that hard to engineer. Moderate-to-high confidence Amorim by submission.
